== Biography ==
Robert Glasgow was baptised on 13 February 1735 at Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian. The named father was James Glasgow; the mother is not recorded in the held indexes. His exact birth date is unknown.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow and father Andrew, miller at Calder, 1772 ===
Robert Glasgow is listed as son of Andrew Glasgow, miller at Calder, in an Edinburgh magistrates’ notice dated 28 November 1772.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395731868/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1772-11-28, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395732022/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1772-11-30, p.3].</ref>

The notice directly identifies its Robert as the son of Andrew, miller at Calder. It does not distinguish East from West Calder or identify the mother. The two newspaper issues repeat the same family statement, not independent evidence of the later profile identities.

Identifying the 1772 Robert with [[Glasgow-1445|this Robert]] remains unresolved. The generation and Calder locality permit comparison, but the 1735 baptism names father James whereas the 1772 notice names father Andrew. This is a recorded father-name conflict for the proposed child-to-adult identification, not merely a doubtful tree attachment. The 57% assessment of adult [[Glasgow-1547|James Glasgow]] does not remove that conflict. The tree sibling [[Glasgow-3052|Andrew Glasgow]] does not resolve it. No alternative parent, person or explanation is adopted; independent identifying evidence is needed before equating these accounts.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, Edinburgh prisoner report, 1767 ===
An Edinburgh city-gaol report names Robert Glasgow among prisoners convicted of theft and reports their sentence of public exposure and banishment from the city and liberties forever.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395727807/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1767-12-21, p.3].</ref>

The report gives no age, family or later outcome identifying the prisoner. It does not establish that he was Robert, son of Andrew the Calder miller, named in 1772.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1445]]. Uncertain birth before 13 February 1735 at Kirknewton/East Calder permits an adult in Edinburgh in 1767. No criminal-record identifier joins him to this prisoner.

=== Supplementary detailed baptism transcript — 4 November 2026 ===

The detailed OPR derivative indexes an unnamed Glasgow child baptised on 13 February 1735 at Kirknewton and East Calder, naming father James Glasgow. It gives OPR 689/20, item 1, with register coverage 1642–1737; it supplies no mother or exact birth date.<ref name="Robert1735Detailed">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4474348 unnamed Glasgow child, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4474348], baptism 13 February 1735, father James Glasgow, Kirknewton and East Calder, OPR 689/20, item 1, register range 1642–1737. Child forename indexed as a dash; mother not supplied. Provider derivative transcript inspected 4 November 2026; original register uninspected.</ref>

The two held companion indexes R_686207970 and R_691904286 explicitly name the child Robert and give the same exact baptism date, parish and father. Those details identify this receipt with Robert's existing baptism event. Its blank forename does not define another child, and the register coverage is not the event's date range. The separate companion residence Kirknewton is not a literal field in this detailed receipt. The three derivatives describe one event, not independent witnesses.

The existing adult father comparison [[Glasgow-1547|James Glasgow]] remains assessed at 57% possible. The literal father name is now available in the held parish derivatives, so the older statement that no parent wording was quoted is superseded for that narrow source question. It does not uniquely identify the adult James or supply a mother. No parent attachment or percentage changes. The 1767 prisoner and 1772 Robert, son of Andrew the Calder miller, remain separate later-life comparisons; this baptism does not establish those adult identities.

An earlier opening placed Robert's birth “before 1735” and described his father as James Glasgow “(~1715)”. Those inherited estimates are not established by the baptism. The current James profile has its own separately assessed childhood account; no replacement father birth year is inferred here. Robert's existing birth bound and family fields are unchanged; a baptism date alone is not an exact birthday.
